title: Decomposition of Evidence, Contradiction, and Fragility in Perturbation Responses
abstract: arXiv:2608.12935v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Perturbation methods explain model decisions by measuring prediction changes under altered inputs, but response magnitude tells us only how much a model reacts, not what that reaction means. The same magnitude can support the final factual-counterfactual difference, oppose it, or arise strongly along the perturbation path yet vanish at the endpoint. We therefore track how the contrast develops as paired inputs are progressively revealed, using the final contrast to interpret the trajectory. We introduce DECAF (Decomposition of Evidence, Contradiction, And Fragility), which routes aligned, opposed, and endpoint-null responses into evidence E, contradiction C, and fragility F. The decomposition preserves ordinary magnitude exactly, Abs = E + C + F, and is unique under endpoint-relative axioms. tldr: 本文提出DECAF方法，将扰动响应分解为证据、矛盾和脆弱性三个独立分量，精确保留总幅度并唯一确定，以区分响应在支持、反对或无效于最终决策时的不同含义。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DECAF, decomposing perturbation responses into evidence, contradiction, and fragility components that exactly preserve total magnitude and are uniquely determined, distinguishing whether responses support, oppose, or are null for the final decision.
